_comment: Per-path review rules for alibaba/open-code-review (the `ocr` CLI). Added 2026-09-26.
Every rule below comes from a defect that actually shipped in this repo, not from a
general style preference -- see the commit that added this file for each one.
Run by hand: ocr delegate preview --from main --to HEAD, then ocr delegate rule <files>.
Nothing here runs on a schedule; David's rule is no automation (docs/plans/PLAN-loops.md).

rules.rule: GENERATED OUTPUT -- do not review this file's contents. Every page and CSV under site/leads/ is written by tooling/seo/build_pages.py and overwritten on the next run, so a comment here cannot be acted on. Review the generator instead. If the output looks wrong, the finding belongs against build_pages.py.
GENERATED OUTPUT -- do not review this file's contents. Written by site/data/build_data.py from the records in propertystack/data/. Review build_data.py instead.

This script decides what a reader is shown about where a number came from, and the site's central claim is that every row names the public record it came from. Enforce:

## Reader-facing URLs
- Any URL that can reach a page, a CSV or an outreach pack MUST pass through _safe_href(). On 2026-09-26, 446 rows carried an href with literal backslashes and a space in it -- Dallas County publishes its bulk link with a Windows path as the query value. run_area._safe_url() had been fixed for the fetcher; the display copy had not, so the raw string went into 449 hrefs. Flag any new source path that bypasses _safe_href().
- A source URL must be absolute and start with http:// or https://.

## Source labels
- No label may be uninformative: "Website", "Link", "Source", "URL" and "Record" alone tell a reader nothing, and "Website" was the label on a 212 MB county zip.
- If the link hands over a file rather than a page, the label MUST name the format, e.g. "(ZIP)" or "(XLSX)".
- Derive a file extension from the regex match, never by rsplit(".") on the whole URL -- a dot in the query string wins that split and produced labels like "Bulk records (DEF)".

## Honesty
- A blank field means the public record is silent. Never substitute zero, a guess, or an inferred value. Flag any new default that could be mistaken for a fact.

Generates the 18 static pages, their CSVs and the home page's pre-JavaScript block. Enforce:

## The page ceiling
- The page count is a deliberate defence against Google's March 2026 scaled-content-abuse demotion, which is SITEWIDE rather than per page. Flag any change that would generate a page per building, or that lowers CITY_MIN far enough to mass-produce thin pages. Evidence: docs/plans/PLAN-seo-geo-strategy.md.

## Claims on the page must be computed
- Every number a page states about itself comes from its own rows. Flag a hard-coded count, date or place name. On 2026-09-26 the opening-2027-2028 page said "in Texas and Arizona" four times while holding 89 buildings all in Texas and none in Arizona, because the place was passed as a literal -- and that text is also FAQPage schema, so Google could surface it.
- The page must not promise more verification than the source links deliver: only ~9% of rows link the building's own record.

## Schema
- A Dataset's contentSize, its ItemList numberOfItems and the file on disk must agree. Generate the page and its CSV from one call so they cannot drift.
- Every page repeats the Organization node under the one shared ORG_ID. Declaring a second identity, or referencing an @id declared on no page, both break entity unification.
- Do not add a schema property that points at a page with no readable content. usageInfo pointed at under-the-hood.html until that page turned out to render 8 visible words.

## Home page title
- index.html's title must not claim state coverage; test_g3_t3_data_note.py and test_g3_freshness.py both assert "Texas & Arizona" is absent. It is a product rule -- work around it, never change those tests.

The guard that strips any link no tool returned, so the agent cannot hand a visitor an invented URL. Enforce:

## Allowlist matching
- An allowlist predicate MUST match on a URL boundary, never a bare prefix. _is_repo() used startswith() and therefore approved github.com/Pu11en/realpage-not-ours and .../realpageXYZ -- everything the allowlist approves skips the check that a tool returned the link, so a look-alike got a free pass. Require equality or the base plus "/".
- Any URL added to the allowlist must resolve. under-the-hood.html sat in it after the page was deleted, which would have meant citing a 404.

## Coverage
- A link the agent is instructed to "always give" (see hermes-profile/SOUL.md) must be allowlisted, or the guard silently removes it. github.com was in no allowlist for weeks while SOUL.md told the agent to always give the repo link.

The suite is the only gate on this repo -- there is no CI, by decision. Enforce:

## No assertion that cannot fail
- Flag `assert X if COND else True`: when COND is false the statement is `assert True` and the test proves nothing. Two shipped on 2026-09-26, guarded on a key that lives on a different schema node and on a byte comparison that is always false on Windows.
- Flag an assertion whose subject is always empty, and a parametrised test whose parameter list can be empty without failing.

## Tests describe behaviour, not implementation
- A test that asserts the exact template or string that produced a value breaks on harmless refactors and teaches everyone to ignore red. Three did: they pinned an account wall two commits had deliberately removed, and a ternary that had become a plain string.

## A missing tool skips, a broken product fails
- Node, Caddy and Docker are absent on David's Windows machine. A test needing one must skip with a reason, and honour CRANESIGNAL_REQUIRE_TOOLS=1 to turn that skip back into a failure. A suite that can never be green is a suite nobody reads.

## Tests must not dirty the working tree
- A generator under test writes to tmp_path, never into the repo.
